title: The Three-Qubit Bit-Flip Code
summary: The three-qubit bit-flip code, syndrome measurement and the threshold.
objectives: Spread one qubit over three with two CNOT gates and explain why this is not copying
Read the position of a single bit flip from two parities, without measuring the data qubits
Correct a single flip with gates controlled by the syndrome
Work out the logical error rate 3p² − 2p³ and the range of p where the code helps
mission: A bit flip is the simplest error to fight, and three qubits are enough to do it. Encode qubit 0 into three qubits (encode), store the syndrome in two ancillas without measuring the data qubits, and correct the flipped qubit (recover). The logical state must survive an X error on any one of the three qubits, for any input state. The code must also reproduce the theory for noise: when every qubit suffers a bit flip with probability p = 0.1, the logical state survives with probability 1 − 3p² + 2p³ = 0.972, against 0.9 for an unprotected qubit.

prediction.question: The input is |0⟩, encoded as |000⟩, and X errors hit qubits 0 and 1. What do the three data qubits hold after the recovery?
options: |111⟩, the logical |1⟩: the recovery flips qubit 2 as well
|000⟩: the syndrome sees both flips and undoes them
A mixture of |000⟩ and |111⟩, because the syndrome cannot say which qubit to fix
prediction.explanation: The parities of qubits 0, 1 and of qubits 1, 2 are 0 and 1, the syndrome of a single flip on qubit 2. The syndrome is a definite pair of bits, so the recovery applies X to qubit 2 with certainty, and all three qubits are flipped: a logical X, not a mixture. The code corrects one flip, not two.

hints: The encoded state has to be entangled, not copied. What happens to |000⟩ and |111⟩ if you apply a CNOT from qubit 0 to qubit 1 and another from qubit 0 to qubit 2 to α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ on qubit 0?

The syndrome is two parities. Ancilla 3 gets CNOTs from qubits 0 and 1, ancilla 4 gets CNOTs from qubits 1 and 2. Work out the two bits for X on each data qubit: they must be different for the three qubits (10, 11 and 01).

For the correction, qml.Toffoli(wires=[3, 4, target]) fires when both ancillas are 1. For a pattern with a 0, apply qml.PauliX to that ancilla before and after the Toffoli. Once recover() fixes every single flip, the noisy case follows by itself.
